title: Brownian Motion in Orthogonal and Symplectic Groups
abstract: Matrix Brownian motion provides a powerful framework for studying crossover ensembles in quantum chaos and quantum transport, as well as thermalization and information scrambling in many-body dynamics. Here, we develop a unified diagrammatic framework to characterize Brownian ensembles for orthogonal and symplectic random matrices, which describe systems with particle-hole symmetry. We compute polynomial averages up to fourth order and construct an orthogonally invariant interpolation for the disconnected $\mathrm{SO}^-(q)$ sector of the orthogonal group. We consider applications relating to the fields of quantum information, quantum chaos, and quantum transport.
summary: This paper develops a unified diagrammatic framework to calculate the time evolution of moment operators for Brownian motion on orthogonal and symplectic Lie groups. By extending techniques from unitary ensembles, it derives explicit formulas for these moments up to fourth order. This work is vital for analyzing quantum chaos, thermalization, and transport in systems with particle-hole symmetry.
main_problem: The paper develops a unified diagrammatic framework to characterize Brownian ensembles for orthogonal and symplectic random matrices.
main_result: Explicit, complex formulas are derived for the time evolution of moment operators ($U_k(t)$) and their corresponding trace moments ($	ext{Tr}(V^k)$) up to fourth order.
method: The calculation uses diagrammatic techniques based on extending methods from unitary ensembles to orthogonal and symplectic cases, involving tensor algebra and matrix exponentiation.
model_or_system: The study concerns Brownian motion on the orthogonal $O(q)$ and symplectic $	ext{Sp}(q)$ groups. The dynamics are governed by moment operators derived from random matrices constrained by an antiunitary involution Z.
key_observables: Moment operators ($U_k(t)$), trace moments ($	ext{Tr}(V^k)$), spectral form factor, and frame potential.
important_parameters: The dimension parameter $q$, the time variable $t$, and the order of the moment $k$ (up to 4).
main_assumptions: The method relies on treating the problem using an antiunitary involution Z to unify the orthogonal and symplectic cases, and involves advanced tensor algebra related to the Brauer algebra.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows diagrammatic representations and multiplication rules for basis tensors in the orthogonal case; Figure 2 does the same for the symplectic case.
paper_structure: The paper builds systematically by calculating moment operators $U_k(t)$ and trace moments recursively, first establishing the general framework (k=1, 2) and then providing explicit, highly complex formulas for higher orders (k=3, k=4).
why_interesting: This work provides powerful mathematical tools derived from random matrix theory that describe quantum dynamics in systems possessing specific symmetries (orthogonal/symplectic), which is crucial for understanding transport and chaos.
